a: Off the coast of the United States, an extensive network of buoys is maintained by the National Data Buoy Center, with the United States Coast Guard handling their deployment and upkeep. a: Towns in the eastern Dominican Republic began making preparations for tens of thousands of refugees, and by 16 January hospitals near the border had been filled beyond capacity with Haitians. By 17 January some reported that they had exhausted supplies of essential medical materials such as antibiotics. Dominican soldiers reinforced the border, and the Dominican Republic's government declared that any Haitians who crossed for medical care would be permitted to remain only on a temporary basis. A local governor remarked, "We have a great desire and we will do everything humanly possible to help Haitian families. But we have our limitations with respect to food and medicine. We need the helping hand of other countries in the area."

a: A great deal of Sholay was filmed in the rocky landscape around Ramanagara, a town near Bangalore in Karnataka. To reach the sets more easily, the filmmakers had to construct a road linking the Bangalore highway to Ramanagara. Art director Ram Yedekar erected an entire township on the location. A prison set was also built outdoors near Rajkamal Studio in Mumbai so that its natural lighting would match that of the on-location shoots. For a time, one section of Ramanagara was known as "Sippy Nagar" in honor of the film's director. As of 2010, tourists passing through Ramanagara were still offered a visit to the "Sholay rocks," where much of the film was shot.
h: Much of Sholay was shot in the rocky terrain of Ramanagara, a town near Bangalore, Karnataka. One part of Ramanagara was for a time called " Sippy Nagar " as a tribute to the director of the film. As of 2010, a visit to the " Sholay rocks " (where much the film was shot) was still being offered to tourists travelling through Ramanagara.

a: No. 2 Group, which had been formed on 20 November 1939, was reorganized on 7 March 1940 into one of the first two area commands, designated Central Area. Based in Sydney, Central Area Command was placed in charge of every Air Force unit in New South Wales apart from those located in the southern Riverina and the northern part of the state. Queensland units were likewise assigned to it on a temporary basis until Northern Area could be established. The command's first AOC was Air Commodore Adrian "King" Cole, who had previously commanded No. 2 Group, while his senior air staff officer was Wing Commander Alan Charlesworth.
h: No. 2 Group, which had been established on 20 November 1939, was re-formed as one of the first two area commands, Central Area, on 7 March 1940. Headquartered in Sydney, Central Area Command was given control of all Air Force units in New South Wales except those in the southern Riverina and the north of the state. Units in Queensland were also temporarily assigned to its control, pending the formation of Northern Area. Central Area's inaugural AOC was Air Commodore Adrian " King " Cole, who had also led No. 2 Group. His senior air staff officer was Wing Commander Alan Charlesworth.
